sources.finding: v1.0.20 records base-commit tracking and recovery for instances whose tmux server/session died.

sources.title: Claude Squad session/storage.go
sources.finding: Source inspection links the session UI to JSON persistence of title, path, branch, status, program, worktree identity and diff stats via SaveInstances/LoadInstances. This is session persistence, not a separate issue tracker.

sources.title: Claude Squad session/instance.go
sources.locator: FromInstanceData; Start; Pause; Resume; SendPrompt; PreviewFullHistory
sources.finding: Source inspection of the documented pause/resume flow shows restoration of stored instances and tmux connections. Missing tmux sessions become Paused; Resume rebuilds missing worktrees and starts or restores tmux. SendPrompt sends terminal keys; PreviewFullHistory captures tmux scrollback. No recovery fixture was run.

sources.title: Claude Squad official repository description
sources.finding: Official repository describes managing multiple AI terminal agents like Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Amp. README separately documents configurable -p commands and named program profiles.

sources.title: Claude Squad README
sources.locator: Installation (Homebrew and Manual) sections, commit ce1ffb4
sources.finding: Claude Squad installs as the cs binary through Homebrew or a public install script; the README names no price, account or paid plan.

sources.title: Claude Squad homepage
sources.finding: The homepage gives Homebrew and shell-script installation and states the software is licensed under GNU AGPL v3.0. It shows no pricing or paid plan.

sources.title: Claude Squad tmux session start
sources.finding: Each session runs the configured program command (default claude) unmodified inside a new tmux session in the task worktree, so the installed agent CLI uses its own stored sign-in.

sources.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 release
sources.finding: The public release provides darwin, linux and windows archives for amd64 and arm64. The application is a terminal UI using tmux and git, not a standalone graphical desktop app.

sources.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
sources.locator: Go source in app, cmd, config, session and ui; web app boilerplate
sources.finding: The executable is a local Bubble Tea terminal UI that creates and attaches tmux sessions, sends prompts and renders diffs. The repository has no product web-session interface, native phone app, human account/member system, SSO integration or telemetry configuration. The web directory is website boilerplate, not a released session client.

sources.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
sources.locator: InstanceData; SaveInstances; session/instance.go; app event handlers
sources.finding: Persistent InstanceData stores session title, path, branch, status, program, worktree and diff state. Human UI actions create sessions. There is no separate issue/task store, product coordinator role/delegation tool, schedule/webhook starter or team user input transport. AutoYes acknowledges prompts in an existing session rather than starting a new task.

sources.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
sources.locator: TmuxSession.Start; session/git/worktree*.go; config and command launcher
sources.finding: The app runs tmux new-session on its current host with a Git worktree as cwd. Built-in execution has no vendor compute provisioner, container runtime or VM launcher. Tmux detachment preserves processes only while that execution host stays running.

sources.title: Claude Squad v1.0.20 source
sources.finding: PushChanges commits, pushes/syncs the branch with git/gh repo sync and optionally opens gh browse --branch. Bounded inspection of the Git/session action code found no PR create/update/review/merge management call.

sources.locator: intro, usage, menu, configuration, profiles, how it works (v1.0.20, ce1ffb4392b0)
sources.finding: Terminal app managing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other local agents such as Aider in tmux sessions and git worktrees; -p sets the program, profiles name launch commands; key menu for new, prompt, kill, attach, push, checkout, resume.

sources.title: claude-squad main.go at v1.0.20
sources.finding: cs must run inside a git repository; --autoyes launches a background daemon on exit; program comes from -p, a profile or the default; a running daemon is stopped at start.

sources.title: claude-squad config/config.go at v1.0.20
sources.finding: Config holds default_program, auto_yes, daemon_poll_interval, branch_prefix and named profiles; default program is the claude command; branch prefix is the lower-cased user name.

sources.title: claude-squad session/instance.go at v1.0.20
sources.finding: Instance statuses are Running, Ready, Loading and Paused; an instance stores title, path, branch, program, auto-yes flag, initial prompt and diff stats.

sources.title: claude-squad session/instance.go at v1.0.20
sources.finding: Pausing commits dirty changes locally, removes the worktree and keeps the branch; an orphaned worktree is pruned and the instance parked as Paused for Resume.

sources.title: claude-squad session/tmux/tmux.go at v1.0.20

sources.finding: Starts a tmux session with a 2 s wait and sets a 10,000-line history limit for scrollback.
